builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
summary: COTEX replaces full fine-tuning of a multimodal agent when adding a new specialist vision tool: it trains small adapters constrained to directions that trigger the call and select the tool without disturbing existing tool choices, plus a protocol that converts task-specific annotations into verified tool-use trajectories. The cost is adapter-level training and the engineering of the trajectory-verification pipeline; it requires a locally trainable open agent rather than a closed API model. It can fail if the verified trajectories are noisy or unrepresentative, and the orthogonal constraint does not guarantee zero interference, so existing tool behavior must be re-validated after each extension.
rationale: Adapter-level tool addition is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU with an open agent, but the benefit is specific to multimodal workloads that actually need specialist vision models, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot rather than direct adoption.

claims.statement: COTEX replaces full fine-tuning of a multimodal agent when adding a new specialist vision tool: it trains small adapters constrained to directions that trigger the call and select the tool without disturbing existing tool choices, plus a protocol that converts task-specific annotations into verified tool-use trajectories. The cost is adapter-level training and the engineering of the trajectory-verification pipeline; it requires a locally trainable open agent rather than a closed API model. It can fail if the verified trajectories are noisy or unrepresentative, and the orthogonal constraint does not guarantee zero interference, so existing tool behavior must be re-validated after each extension.
Gains on ten vision-language benchmarks after adding three specialist tools, with at most a 0.3-point drop on existing tool performance.
